implementedScope: NexoWatt product branding on principal login, portal and UI assets; technical identifiers, upstream provenance and license attribution retained.
Host enrollment validates a bounded root-owned accounts input, unique identities and initial credentials, canonical membership and private account/group ACLs.
Service/Admin is reserved to the root-provisioned administrator role; installer and end-user accounts choose their own password and cannot promote roles through browser APIs.
Admin and UI enforce exactly one active canonical role, current account/session revision and mandatory first password before product access.
Protected UI reads require authentication; scoped own-password handlers reject target/role injection; password KDF work is bounded and authorization is rechecked.
SSE authorization is checked for each frame; revoked/logout sessions close their own streams; protected data has no service-worker cache fallback.
Actual WebSocket dispatch denies non-Service raw object/state/file subscriptions and administration; exact reviewed transport transformation bounds inbound frames to 1 MiB.
Root-owned signed admission/profile gates remain the intended route for additional adapters; arbitrary browser package/code installation is not enabled.
Architecture, account contracts, threat documentation, build provenance and runtime/source CycloneDX inventories accompany the development stand.

roles.authority: Exactly one canonical active membership; user/group ownership remains with host enrollment. Generic controller ACL privileges are denied to non-Service roles.

openReleaseGates.detail: Final test:all exited 1 at 99-peer 250-ms lease timing assertion (round 4 stale_or_invalid_lease). Exactly one separate final mesh invocation passed at P95 92/max121 ms for 792 responses. No deadline relaxed, no test bypass, no established cause; this diagnostic does not close the failed required-suite gate. Controlled investigation and target performance acceptance remain required.
Controller object APIs provide no cross-adapter atomic compare-and-swap for simultaneous password resets. Rechecks and narrow writes reduce races; operational coordination remains required.
Shared process/database authority remains. TLS and root-owned code do not isolate a compromised adapter; per-adapter identities and least-privilege separation need their own acceptance.
Debian 12 Lite, systemd without root, VMware and Raspberry Pi 5 with 8/16 GB and SSD require installation/reboot/recovery/performance and networking validation.
Tailscale enrollment, ACLs, MFA/service access, revocation and required LAN/VLAN reachability need a concrete target network test; accepting every network is not an authorization policy.

Devices, EEBUS, OCPP and Backup activation, encrypted protocol configuration, safe failure/recovery and physical functions remain outside this two-adapter lab acceptance. Existing findings in those components are not closed by this work. Mesh exchange/energy currently require the product login boundary; unattended M2M remains blocked and no machine-identity implementation is claimed.
Final npm findings require disposition; OS/runtime/firmware and frontend attribution gaps remain. Full support/lifecycle, signed update and recovery processes require their own product evidence.

Ordinary account/group events revoke synchronously before socket publication; missed events also rely on a five-second watchdog. No instantaneous distributed revocation or rollback of already running commands is claimed.

This engineering evidence does not establish CRA conformity, CE authorization, IEC 62443 certification or a safety certification. Product scope, applicable requirements/standards, manufacturer risk assessment, lifecycle/support, vulnerability process, technical file and conformity procedure remain manufacturer responsibilities requiring separately validated evidence.
No external independent penetration test or certification; source review by cooperating AI agents is identified as such.

finalizationRule: Final r2 integration, current UI outcome (required full suite failed), SBOM/replay, package/source comparison and bounded secret evidence are linked to exact files. Earlier r1/component snapshots remain historical. Source Git/outer ZIP checks are separate root evidence. No production release follows from this report.

testGateMigrationReview.executionClaim: Source/diff inspection plus git diff --check. The final npm run test:all subsequently failed at the unchanged 99-peer mesh timing gate; migration review does not convert it into a pass.

scope.assessment: Existing TS source/import/runtime helper assertions retained; main-runtime contract now requires central client and eos-admin management while rejecting retired local secret/evaluator/expected-key paths.

Logo/layout/runtime checks retained. The obsolete protected-page/pre-cache assumption is replaced by executing the actual SW public-asset predicate: public logo allowed, display HTML and API JSON denied.

Bootstrap helper cases retained; source gates require prior login, exact account-recovery list, central lease, license.manage protection, local-save HTTP409, no browser key persistence and continued preview control lock.

Only the issuer fixture migrates to central getStatus/isAllowed. Existing signed/split, pool/group allocation, stale status, downgrade, disabled-slot, configuration migration and API save/import limit assertions retained; new negative checks deny forged retired local flags.

The existing ephemeral scripts/eos-tls-fixture.cjs helper is now included for the shipped access test; no new product dependency or runtime entrypoint is introduced by that addition. Focused account/SSE/SW suite is added to test:all.

Read to verify helper scope: creates temporary local EC test certificate/key, bounds HTTPS response size/deadline/redirects and cleans temporary directory on exit; no embedded private key and no product runtime import observed in reviewed call sites.

Read-only diff/full-script review: canonical initialized account harness and real login provide installer session; central Pro lease fixture replaces retired local flags. Anonymous/stale customer sessions remain HTTP401 for exchange/energy before and after activation, with legacy authEnabled true and false. After valid installer login the existing app lifecycle HTTP404/423/409, invalid HMAC HTTP403, 70k/170k body HTTP413, key-redaction, pairing, accounting and active deinstallation/save protections remain asserted. No HMAC/size/lifecycle assertion removed, no product runtime edit.

limits: Static source assertions supplement, but do not replace, actual authentication/lease/preview tests.
No product runtime implementation edits were made during this review.
Package/helper closure and final suite must be bound to the final candidate; historical component report package hash is not silently reused.

Mesh protocol checks with a browser-session fixture are not an unattended M2M acceptance or production design. The current preview blocks unattended exchange/energy access; future machine identities require separate authorization/encryption work.
